lines.text: - Not decided: whether the person's typed yes at a pinned checkpoint is a way past of its own kind, or a stop kept on purpose (#992).
- Not decided: whether each machine wall, such as a pre-flight halt or a stop condition, is a gate that needs a way past, or evidence that stays enforced.
- Not decided: which shortcuts are guarded first; #893 leaves open "Which paths and which plays the hook covers, and how a person overrides it on purpose."
- Not decided: whether the way past is the coding tool's own prompt, a word typed in the session, or a line in the pull request that the review reads.
- Not decided: in a run with no person present, such as a scheduled run, whether a guardrail's refusal counts as stopping a person, and whether the run may pass it on its own.

- Not decided: whether a guardrail that fails or times out lets the action through, or is set to block on failure; a hook that fails or times out "does not block unless the hook is set to block on failure".
- Not decided: whether the guard on the evals folder, which keeps a builder agent from the evals, has a way past.
- Not decided: who reads the list: every play at its start, the plan views, or only Learn.
- Not decided: whether an entry is also an issue in the team's tracker, under the work that made it.
- Not decided: who closes an entry: only a person, the play that does the owed work, or either.
- Not decided: whether the places that name what is owed today, such as a plan session's commit, the thin marks, an upgrade's report and initialize's record, also write an entry, or stay as they are.
- Not decided: whether the person's typed yes at a pinned checkpoint is a way past of its own kind, or a stop kept on purpose (#992).
- Not decided: whether a person may give a pinned yes with something still to be done, kept as an owed entry.
- Not decided: whether some pinned yeses need a second person's yes.

- .garura/product/product-os/software-delivery-planning/ship-every-change/capability.md: "Not decided: whether the merge's typed yes is the way past the merge's checkpoint that Orchestration's Must not asks for, or a stop kept on purpose (#992)."
- .garura/product/product-os/features/fn-673/feature.md: "Not decided: whether the typed yes is the way past this checkpoint that Orchestration's Must not asks for, or a stop kept on purpose (#992)."
- Not decided: whether the skip's record is a line in the issue's gate ledger, which the learner reads, or a record of its own beside it.
- Not decided: whether a skip by the settings is also owed, kept by Keep what is owed with the work that made it (fn-keep-what-is-owed), or only a record.
- Not decided: whether the record also names the machine checks that carried the checkpoint, and their results.
- Not decided: whether each machine wall, such as a pre-flight halt, a sensitive-file block or a stop condition, is a gate that needs a way past, or evidence that stays enforced.
- Not decided: whether every way past must carry the person's reason, or who and when are enough.
- Not decided: whether a way past expires after a time, or stays owed until it is paid.
- Not decided: the way past of each gate on today's list; #992 leaves it to its ADR, "each with what its key would record or why it keeps a human beat".
